title: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
description: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT undoes everything done since that savepoint was created, WITHOUT ending the transaction - unlike a plain ROLLBACK, which would undo everything. Set a savepoint named `before_mistake`, then (by mistake) delete EVERY row from `appointments`. Roll back to `before_mistake` to undo that. Then correctly delete only the appointments with status `'cancelled'`.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
Four statements in order: the SAVEPOINT, the mistaken unconditional DELETE, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT (undoing only that mistaken DELETE), then a second, correctly-filtered DELETE.
Create the savepoint, delete every row, roll back to that exact savepoint name, then delete again with a WHERE status = 'cancelled' filter this time.
expected_behavior: appointments ends up with every row EXCEPT the cancelled one or ones - the mistaken full delete never actually took effect, but the correct, filtered delete did.
solution: SAVEPOINT before_mistake; DELETE FROM appointments; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT before_mistake; DELETE FROM appointments WHERE status = 'cancelled';
explanation: This is exactly the real-world use case for ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT: you tried something, realized it was wrong, undid just that part, and kept working in the same transaction instead of starting over.

hidden_tests.label: only the cancelled appointment is gone
